cards.subject: Our Lady of Mercy in the Mercedarian image, composed for the arched window. Our Lady stands at the centre, half-length and a little above the other figures, in the white habit of the Order of Mercy: a white tunic, a white scapular and a wide white mantle, a white veil, a small gold crown; on the breast of her scapular the small shield of the Order (a white cross on a red field above upright red and gold bars, no letters). In her right hand a slender gold sceptre; with her left arm she spreads her open white mantle wide over the captives who kneel beneath it, and from that hand hangs a small white scapular offered to them. Under the mantle, small and half-length, three captives in plain, worn clothes turn their faces up to her, their hands joined; a broken iron chain and an opened shackle lie before them on the ground. Behind, the harbour of Barcelona in soft morning light: a stone quay, a tall-masted galley at anchor, the sea and a clear sky. Serene and devotional: no wounds, no suffering shown, only relief. No lettering anywhere; keep the mantle and every figure inside the arched window.
cards.face: Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md, a young woman of about eighteen with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre under a white inner veil and a blue mantle drawn over the head — here the veil and mantle are white, not blue, and she looks down with tenderness at the captives. The captives are small and clearly different: a North African-born Christian sailor of about forty with a LEAN, LONG face, a hooked nose, dark sun-browned skin and a short black beard; a young mother of about twenty-five with a ROUND, soft face and a dark headscarf, holding a small child; an old man of about seventy with a NARROW, bony face, a bald crown and white stubble.
cards.basis: The image is the one the Order of Mercy fixed from the sixteenth century: Our Lady in the white Mercedarian habit with the Order's shield, sceptre and crown, sheltering the ransomed captives under her mantle, broken chains at their feet. Her face is the set's.

cards.subject: The gift of the Rosary to St. Dominic, composed for the arched window. Our Lady sits enthroned on a bank of golden cloud at the upper right, half-length, in a rose-red gown and her blue mantle over a white veil, a small gold crown on her head; on her left knee the Christ Child in a white shift, and with her right hand she holds out a rosary of dark wooden beads with a small gold cross, letting it fall toward St. Dominic. The Child also holds out a second rosary toward him. St. Dominic kneels at the lower left, half-length, in the white habit and black cappa of his Order, his face lifted to her, both hands reaching up to receive the beads; a white lily lies on the ground beside him. Behind, the hill country of Languedoc near Prouille: green slopes, a small stone chapel with a bell-cote, cypresses, and a clear blue sky with a few small child-angels' heads in the cloud around Our Lady. No lettering anywhere; keep the cloud and both figures inside the arched window.
cards.face: Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md: a young woman of about eighteen with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre under a white inner veil and a blue mantle drawn over the head; she looks down at St. Dominic with a gentle smile. The Christ Child as in recurring-figures.md, about two years old: a plump, ROUND child's face with full rosy cheeks, a high rounded forehead, a small button nose, large clear brown eyes, a small rosy mouth, soft short golden-brown curls; fair, glowing skin; a plain gold halo. St. Dominic as on the dominic card: a man of about thirty-five with a gentle, OVAL face — a straight, fine nose, soft brown eyes under level brows, a calm closed mouth; short brown hair in a monastic tonsure (a ring of short curls around a shaven crown), a short trimmed brown beard; a white habit and scapular under a black cappa and hood; the same face as that card, raised in wonder. The three must read as clearly different: the Mother young and fair under her blue mantle, the Child round and golden-curled, Dominic a tonsured, bearded friar in black and white.
cards.basis: Our Lady giving the rosary to St. Dominic, often with the Child giving a second one, is the standard image of the feast since the sixteenth century (Sassoferrato's Madonna del Rosario at Santa Sabina, Murillo, Caravaggio's Rosary Madonna). Dominic keeps the face of his own card.

cards.subject: The Holy House of Nazareth carried through the night sky by angels, composed for the arched window. At the centre, a small, plain house of rough reddish-brown and grey stone with a low pitched roof and one small window, borne on a bank of cloud by four angels in white and pale-rose robes with broad white-and-gold wings, two beneath and one at each end, their hands under its walls. Seated on the roof, half-length, Our Lady in her rose-red gown and blue mantle over a white veil, holding the Christ Child on her lap; the Child raises his right hand in blessing toward the land below. Beneath them, small, the dark blue Adriatic Sea under a starry night sky with a first pale glow of dawn at the horizon, and on a green hill by the shore a wood of laurel trees where the house will come to rest. No lettering anywhere; keep the house, the angels and the cloud inside the arched window.
cards.face: Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md: a young woman of about eighteen with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre under a white inner veil and a blue mantle drawn over the head; she looks down at the land with quiet calm. The Christ Child as in recurring-figures.md, about two years old: a plump, ROUND child's face with full rosy cheeks, a high rounded forehead, a small button nose, large clear brown eyes, a small rosy mouth, soft short golden-brown curls; fair, glowing skin; a plain gold halo. The angels are small and secondary, youthful and serene, each different: one with a HEART-SHAPED face and golden curls, one with a LONGER face and straight dark-brown hair, one with a ROUND face and auburn curls, one in profile.
cards.basis: The translation of the Holy House by angels, with Our Lady and the Child seated on its roof, is the image of Loreto in fifteenth- to eighteenth-century painting (the Met's Translation attributed to Saturnino Gatti; Tiepolo's lost Scalzi ceiling). The shrine's own black statue was not used, since the catalog asks for the house borne by angels; Our Lady has the set's face.

cards.subject: The image of Our Lady of Guadalupe as it appears on St. Juan Diego's tilma, painted faithfully and filling the arched window: Our Lady standing, full-length, small within the arch, her head inclined gently to her right, her eyes lowered, her hands joined in prayer before her breast; a rose-pink tunic patterned with small gold flowers and leaves, gathered with a narrow dark sash tied high above the waist, a small gold brooch with a tiny cross at the neck; over all a blue-green mantle edged with gold and scattered with small gold stars, drawn over her head. She stands on a dark crescent moon held up by a small angel with wings of green, white and red feathers, his arms spread holding her mantle and tunic. Behind her the full golden sunburst of straight and wavy rays in an almond-shaped glory, edged by soft white-and-blue clouds. The ground of the window around the glory is the warm, faintly woven natural cream of the maguey-fibre cloth, with a few Castilian roses at the lower corners. Juan Diego does not appear (he has his own card holding the tilma). No lettering anywhere; keep the whole image inside the arched window.
cards.face: The image's own face, not the set's Our Lady: a young Mexican woman of about sixteen with warm olive-brown skin and a small, softly OVAL, slightly elongated face — a straight, gentle nose, lowered dark eyes under fine dark brows, a small closed mouth with a faint serene smile, a smooth rounded chin; straight dark-brown hair parted in the centre and falling beneath the mantle; her head tilted to her right. The angel below: a small child's face with a round chin and short dark curls, looking out.
cards.basis: A Marian title shows its own image: the tilma of 1531 kept at the Basilica of Guadalupe (olive-skinned young woman inclined to her right, hands joined, rose tunic with floral pattern and dark sash, star-strewn blue-green mantle, crescent moon borne by an angel with eagle-feathered wings, golden rays).

sources.title: Wikipedia: Our Lady of Guadalupe (description of the image)
Wikimedia Commons: Virgen de Guadalupe (tilma, Basilica of Guadalupe)

cards.subject: The Immaculate Heart of Mary, half-length, facing the viewer in slight three-quarter view, composed for the arched window. Our Lady in a white gown and her blue mantle over a white veil, her left hand laid on her breast and her right hand gently indicating her heart, which shines on her breast over the gown: a glowing golden-red heart wreathed with a ring of small white roses, a small clear flame rising from its top, soft golden rays around it; no sword, no thorns, no wound. Behind her an enclosed garden in the gold of late afternoon: a low stone wall, white lilies and white roses, a small stone fountain, a slender cypress, and over the wall the soft hills of Galilee under a pale sky. Calm and radiant. No lettering anywhere; keep the figure and garden inside the arched window.
cards.face: Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md: a young woman of about eighteen with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre under a white inner veil and a blue mantle drawn over the head; her gaze lowered and inward, recollected, with the faintest smile.
cards.basis: The devotional image of the Immaculate Heart shows Our Lady pointing to her heart wreathed in roses with a flame above it; the sword of the Sorrows was left off because our_lady_sorrows already carries it. The enclosed garden is the hortus conclusus of Song of Songs 4:12, long read of her. Her face is the set's.

cards.subject: Our Lady entrusted to St. John, the moment after Calvary, composed for the arched window. In the foreground, half-length side by side, Our Lady (left) in a deep blue mantle over a white veil and a rose-red gown, her hands crossed on her breast, her face grave and peaceful; St. John (right) turned toward her, one arm around her shoulders to lead her home and his other hand on his heart, taking her as his mother. Behind them, small and far off on the hill of Golgotha under a dusk sky of violet and gold, the plain silhouette of three wooden crosses, the central one taller; the walls and towers of Jerusalem at the right in the fading light. No body, no wounds, no blood shown: only the distant crosses. Quiet and tender. No lettering anywhere; keep both figures and the hill inside the arched window.
cards.face: Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md, the same face matured (the same woman, not a different face), a woman of about forty-eight with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre under a white inner veil and a blue mantle drawn over the head; eyes lowered in sorrow and trust. St. John as in recurring-figures.md: a beardless young man of about twenty-two with a smooth OVAL face, large upturned brown eyes, a straight nose, a small full mouth; wavy golden-brown hair to the jaw; a green tunic and a red-orange mantle; he looks at her with devotion. The two must read as clearly different: she mature, veiled, in blue; he beardless and golden-haired, in green and red-orange.
cards.basis: The feast's Mass is built on John 19:25-27 (gospel, collect, communion antiphon): at the Cross Christ gave his Mother to the beloved disciple, and in him to the Church. The Cenacle of Acts 1:14 was passed over because the pentecost card already shows Our Lady among the Apostles. Faces from recurring-figures.md.

cards.subject: The boy Jesus found in the Temple of Jerusalem, composed for the arched window. At the centre, seated a little raised on a stone bench in a colonnade of the Temple, the boy Jesus, twelve, in a rose-red tunic, one hand raised as he speaks; around him, half-length, three teachers of the Law in striped prayer shawls and turbans, one holding an open scroll (blank, no writing), listening astonished. At the left, just arriving through the colonnade, Our Lady and St. Joseph, half-length: Mary with her hands stretched toward her son in relief, Joseph behind her with his staff. Tall golden-brown stone columns, a bronze lamp, and beyond them the sunlit courts and walls of the Temple under a clear sky. No lettering anywhere, no letters on the scroll; keep all figures inside the arched window.
cards.face: The Christ Child as in recurring-figures.md, now twelve: the same face lengthened — a softly ROUND, youthful face with rosy cheeks, a high rounded forehead, a small straight nose, large clear brown eyes, a small rosy mouth, golden-brown curls grown to the neck; a plain gold halo; his gaze calm and assured. Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md: a young woman of about thirty with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre under a white inner veil and a blue mantle drawn over the head; eyes wide with relief. St. Joseph as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about forty with a LONG OVAL face — a straight nose, gentle dark-brown eyes under level brows, a quiet mouth; full dark-brown curly hair to the nape and a short full dark-brown beard; a green tunic and an ochre-brown mantle, holding a staff. The three teachers differ clearly: an old man of about seventy-five with a LONG, NARROW face, a high bald forehead, a thin aquiline nose and a long white beard; a heavy man of about fifty-five with a BROAD, SQUARE face, a flat wide nose, bushy black brows and a short grizzled black beard; a younger scribe of about thirty-five with a TRIANGULAR face, sharp cheekbones, a narrow chin and a thin brown beard.
cards.basis: Luke 2:41-51: after three days Mary and Joseph find the twelve-year-old Jesus among the teachers in the Temple. The Child's face grows from the set's Christ Child as recurring-figures.md prescribes for this card.

cards.subject: The Wedding at Cana, composed for the arched window. At the left, half-length, Our Lady in her rose-red gown and blue mantle bends toward a young servant and gestures toward her Son; at the centre Christ, half-length, in his rose-red tunic and blue mantle, raises his right hand in blessing over six large stone water jars standing in a row in the foreground, from one of which a second servant pours a stream of deep red wine into a clay pitcher. At the right, behind a long table with a white cloth, bread, figs and clay cups, the steward in a yellow robe tastes from a cup in surprise, and beside him the young bride in white with a garland of flowers and the groom in a blue robe. A courtyard of a whitewashed Galilean house with a vine-covered pergola and hanging lamps, hills in evening light beyond. Festive and serene. No lettering anywhere; keep all figures and the jars inside the arched window.
cards.face: Christ as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about thirty-three with a LONG OVAL face narrowing gently to the chin — a high, smooth forehead, a long straight nose with a fine bridge, calm almond-shaped dark-brown eyes under level brown brows, high, softly modelled cheekbones, a quiet closed mouth; chestnut-brown hair parted in the centre and falling in soft waves past the shoulders; a short, full chestnut beard and moustache, lightly parted at the chin; a plain gold halo; a rose-red tunic and a blue mantle. Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md, a woman of about forty-six, with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre under a white inner veil and a blue mantle drawn over the head. The others are secondary and clearly different: the servant she speaks to, a lad of about fifteen with a narrow, eager face and short black curls; the pouring servant, a stocky man of about forty with a ROUND, ruddy face and a thick black beard; the steward, about sixty, with a LONG, fleshy face, a bulbous nose, raised grey brows and a short white beard; the bride, about sixteen, a HEART-SHAPED face with dark eyes and dark hair under a white veil; the groom, about twenty, a SQUARE-JAWED face with a first dark beard.
cards.basis: John 2:1-11, the first of the signs, painted as the Western tradition does (Mary's intercession, the six stone jars, the steward tasting). Christ and Our Lady from recurring-figures.md; the disciples were left out to keep the scene legible in the window.

cards.subject: Christ proclaiming the Kingdom on the shore of the Sea of Galilee, composed for the arched window. Christ stands at the centre on a low grassy rise, half-length, in his rose-red tunic and blue mantle, his right hand raised as he speaks and his left open toward the listeners. Before him, smaller, a gathered crowd seated and standing on the slope: at the left Peter and Andrew in fishermen's tunics with a wet net over Andrew's arm, turned toward him; a mother with a small child in her lap; an old shepherd leaning on his staff; a young boy kneeling at the front. Behind, the calm blue lake with two small fishing boats drawn up on the pebbly shore, the brown hills of the far side and a bright morning sky. No lettering anywhere; keep Christ and the crowd inside the arched window.
cards.face: Christ as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about thirty-three with a LONG OVAL face narrowing gently to the chin — a high, smooth forehead, a long straight nose with a fine bridge, calm almond-shaped dark-brown eyes under level brown brows, high, softly modelled cheekbones, a quiet closed mouth; chestnut-brown hair parted in the centre and falling in soft waves past the shoulders; a short, full chestnut beard and moustache, lightly parted at the chin; a plain gold halo; a rose-red tunic and a blue mantle; his gaze earnest and warm, looking at the crowd. St. Peter as in recurring-figures.md: about sixty-five, a broad, weathered fisherman's face, a strong wide nose, deep-set earnest eyes, a lined forehead; curly grey-white hair balding from the back with a curly tuft at the forehead; a short, square, curly grey-white beard; a blue tunic and golden-ochre mantle. St. Andrew as on the andrew card: an old man of about seventy with a kindly, weathered, LONG face — a long nose, deep-set eyes; abundant unruly curly grey-white hair and a long grey-white beard divided at the end into two points; a green tunic and a red mantle. The others are small and different: the mother, about twenty-five, a ROUND, soft face under a brown headscarf; the shepherd, about seventy, a NARROW, bony face with a hooked nose and a thin white beard; the boy, about eight, a heart-shaped face with black curls.
cards.basis: Mark 1:14-20: in Galilee Jesus proclaims that the Kingdom is at hand and calls the fishermen Simon and Andrew by the lake. Christ and Peter from recurring-figures.md; Andrew from his own card.

cards.subject: The Last Supper at the moment of the Institution, composed for the arched window. Christ sits at the centre behind a long table with a white cloth, half-length and facing us, his eyes raised to heaven, holding up in both hands a round, plain unleavened loaf over a simple gold cup of wine; a soft golden light falls on the bread. At his right, St. John, the youngest, leans close against him with his hands joined; at his left, St. Peter bends forward with his hand on his breast. Along the table, smaller and half-length, other Apostles in varied tunics and mantles turn toward him in wonder. On the table a few more loaves, a clay pitcher, a dish with bitter herbs. The upper room of plain stone with a round arch, an oil lamp hanging from a chain, and through a small window the flat roofs of Jerusalem under a deep blue evening sky. Reverent and still. No lettering anywhere, no symbols on the bread; keep all figures inside the arched window.
cards.face: Christ as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about thirty-three with a LONG OVAL face narrowing gently to the chin — a high, smooth forehead, a long straight nose with a fine bridge, calm almond-shaped dark-brown eyes under level brown brows, high, softly modelled cheekbones, a quiet closed mouth; chestnut-brown hair parted in the centre and falling in soft waves past the shoulders; a short, full chestnut beard and moustache, lightly parted at the chin; a plain gold halo; a rose-red tunic and a blue mantle; his eyes lifted in thanksgiving. St. John as in recurring-figures.md: a beardless young man of about twenty-two with a smooth OVAL face, large upturned brown eyes, a straight nose, a small full mouth; wavy golden-brown hair to the jaw; a green tunic and a red-orange mantle. St. Peter as in recurring-figures.md: about sixty-five, a broad, weathered fisherman's face, a strong wide nose, deep-set earnest eyes, a lined forehead; curly grey-white hair balding from the back with a curly tuft at the forehead; a short, square, curly grey-white beard; a blue tunic and golden-ochre mantle. The other Apostles behind, each different: St. Andrew as on the andrew card, an old man with curly grey-white hair and a long grey-white beard forked in two points; St. James the Greater as on the james_greater card, a young man of about twenty-eight with chestnut hair to the jaw and a sparse short beard; St. Thomas as on the thomas_apostle card, a beardless young man of about twenty-five with short dark hair; St. Bartholomew as on the bartholomew card, a man of about forty-five with black curly hair and a long black beard beginning to grey.
cards.basis: The Institution of the Eucharist at the Last Supper (Lk 22:19-20; Mk 14:22-24) with John leaning on the Lord's breast (Jn 13:23), painted at the moment of the blessing of the bread rather than the betrayal, as Juan de Juanes did. Christ, Peter and John from recurring-figures.md; the other Apostles from their cards.
